newsitem.title: USA: Miami area flooded as heavy rains fall.
newsitem.headline: Miami area flooded as heavy rains fall.

text.p: Neighbourhoods were flooded and streets closed around Miami on Tuesday after up to 16 inches (40 cm) of rain fell overnight, forecasters said.

A flood watch was posted for much of southern Florida's tip on Tuesday morning. Forecasters said it could be upgraded to a flood warning later in the day, as a light rain that continued in many areas around the city was expected to get heavier as the day went on.

Forecasters said some of the heavy rains came from a tropical storm in the Pacific last week. "It contributed at least indirectly to some of the rainfall that we had," said forecaster Ed Rappaport at the National Hurricane Centre.
"As of this morning, there had been no development of that system and the weather system that has resulted remains rather poorly organised," he said.
The heaviest flooding appeared to have occurred west and south of the city, including the city of Homestead.
But early reports did not indicate that property damage would be significant, forecasters said.

The National Hurricane Centre was keeping a close eye on a weather system associated with the heavy rains. The remnants of Tropical Storm Andres, which developed in the Pacific last week, had crossed Central America into the southern Gulf of Mexico, sending rains northeast across Florida.
There was no immediate indication that the storm would develop into a tropical depression or become Tropical Storm Ana, the first named storm of the Atlantic hurricane season, forecasters said.
